steps.text: Spread butter on one side of a slice of bread and place it, buttered side down, into a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Spread 1/2 of the pesto sauce on the unbuttered side of the bread. Stack provolone cheese, tomato, and American cheese on top of pesto, in that order.
Spread remaining pesto sauce on second slice of bread. Place it pesto side down onto sandwich in the pan. Butter the top side of bread.
Gently fry sandwich, flipping once, until both sides are golden brown and cheese has melted, about 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto Grilled Cheese Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: An easy pesto sandwich with big flavor. Give your grilled cheese Italian flair by adding provolone cheese, tomato, and pesto to elevate this favorite.

review.reviewBody: With hubs out Christmas shopping it was just me at home for supper tonight. I had presents to wrap and baking to do, so I wanted something simple but delicious, something more interesting than the plain ol' grilled cheese sandwich I almost settled for. Hoping for a twist on that old standby, this recipe came up with a simple search for "grilled cheese sandwich" and what a great find it was! The ingredients seem like such a natural, yet I never would have thought to put them together in a grilled cheese sandwich. I really liked this - the flavors all come together and using good, sturdy Italian bread really helps make the sandwich. This was a quick and delicious meal with ingredients I readily have on hand. No boring grilled cheese sandwich here!
Does not need american cheese at all. Only put Pesto on one slice of bread because it overpowers everything otherwise.
I subbed mozz cheese for the American cheese, and added fresh basil leaves. So so good!!!

LOVED this slightly different rendition of a traditional American sandwich! I used homemade pesto I had made from my basil garden. I did not choose to add any tomatoes this time since the soup I was serving was tomato-based. Each sandwich had 4 medium-sized pieces of cheese--Vermont White Cheddar and Smoked Gouda. I used olive oil instead of butter for frying--this makes very crispy outsides! Will repeat this for sure. All the guys at my table were delighted with these!

Loved it! Kids loved it too. Added fresh spinach just because I had it. Great addition. Also, baked the sandwiches in the toaster oven to save time and used sandwich thin bread to make them healthier. Turned out fantastic. We will definitely make this again.
This is a fantastic sandwich. My only tip: add just a bit of smoked salt and garlic powder to the inside. You won't be disappointed. It's also great with Havarti instead of provolone.
Definitely omit the American cheese, and use half the pesto. I used fontina and DID grill it in butter! The result was a very rich and full flavored grilled cheese, Italian style!

I followed the recipe’s ingredients, grilled on low using a weight….about 5 minutes each side. It was very good but next time I will not use American cheese. For me it didn’t complement the other flavors. Very nice recipe. Thank you. BTW…it goes well with Creamy Tomato Basil soup.

I thought it was very good and very easy!! My husband LOVED it! I would say though the 5 minutes on each side was too long. It took 5 minutes TOTAL on medium low heat. I tried the 5 minutes per side and burned the bread. Thank you!!

Put pesto on both sides of bread then topped with 2 slices of provolone and chopped roasted red peppers (tried to recall recipe from memory alone. LOL!) It was really yummy but only giving it 4 stars bc it wasn't the recipe but close. Didn't really like the provolone. I will try mozz. or Amer next. Def. has potential for a 5 star. Play a little! Update: Made 4-19 much better with Amer. Cheese and provolone, but OMG! I think its 2000 calories at least. Its good but not worth the calories! Have sparingly!

First let me start by warning everyone to check the food they already have in there house, because I came back from the store only to find that my provolone was moldy. Also butter the top slice before putting it on or else the bread may break.
 I substituted the provolone, and yellow american, for two slices of white american cheese. Even with the lack of specified ingredients my family and I loved them! Next time I may stay with my choice of cheese and add a few deli slices of chicken breast. Nothing fancy needed here!
I used pepperjack and cheddar cheese, otherwise I followed the recipe. Simple and delicious.
I added a dash of Dijon mustard. Really kicked the flavor up a notch!
Wonderful sandwich! I’ll definitely make this again.
Tobias

I had a jar of pesto from a gift basket I didn't know what to do with. Then I saw this recipe 2 days ago and have made it twice already. Love it so much! I live far from town so used what I had: thin-sliced whole grain bread, and Swiss instead of provolone. Pesto is now on my shopping list. Will never make grilled cheese without it again. Thank you!
This is a great "go-to" when my husband is out of town and I just want something easy to prepare for myself. Love how the flavors blend together.
I made a second one, adding fresh cilantro! Both were awesome. I liked the cilantro add, a tad bit better!
I changed American cheese to cheddar cheese
the taste
